## Objective
- Improve the physical isometric decor in each property so it looks polished and professionally made, especially the counter.

## Requirements
- Apply the change to the existing game and make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Verify with screenshots saved as small JPEGs (maximum 1280px wide), reading only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Focus on the existing isometric canvas renderer and property-specific props.

## Work State
### Completed
- Located the property layouts and prop definitions in `js/data.js`.
- Identified the render flow, prop renderers, and counter renderer in `js/render.js`.
- Confirmed the repository has no uncommitted changes before implementation.

### Active
- Improve physical props across the five properties, with special attention to the counter.
- Verify the visual changes in-game.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Upgrade counter details and property props in `js/render.js`, using the existing property-specific palettes and prop configurations.
2. Run the game, capture a small JPEG screenshot, inspect the latest screenshot, and adjust as needed.

## Relevant Files
- `js/render.js`: Isometric scene flow, prop renderers, and `drawCounter`.
- `js/data.js`: Layouts, palettes, decor, and physical prop placements for all five properties.
- `index.html`: Game canvas and interface entry point.
- `start.sh`: Starts the game for visual verification.

## Important Context
- Property IDs are `apartment`, `garage`, `lab`, `warehouse`, and `empire`.
- Props are drawn in a depth-sorted queue; shared box geometry is implemented by `box()`.
- No implementation changes or screenshots have been made yet.

- Improve the physical isometric decor across all five properties, especially the counter, so it looks polished and professionally made.

- Apply changes to the existing game using reasonable assumptions.

- Focus on the existing isometric canvas renderer and property-specific props.

3. Capture a JPEG screenshot at no more than 1280px wide, inspect the latest screenshot, and adjust as needed.

- `js/render.js`: Isometric scene flow, depth-sorted prop rendering, shared `box()` geometry, and `drawCounter()`.

- `start.sh`: Starts the game.

- Property IDs are `apartment`, `garage`, `lab`, `warehouse`, and `empire`.
- Props are depth-sorted by `x + y`; the counter is rendered separately via `drawCounter()`.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url

  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page

  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown

  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file

  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs

  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes

DevTools:

## Objective
- Improve the physical isometric decor across all five properties, especially the counter, so it looks polished and professionally made.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game using reasonable assumptions.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs no wider than 1280px, and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Focus on the existing isometric canvas renderer and property-specific props.

## Work State
### Completed
- Located property layouts and prop definitions in `js/data.js`, and renderer flow, prop methods, and `drawCounter()` in `js/render.js`.
- Started the game with `./start.sh`.

### Active
- Improve the counter and physical props across the five properties.
- Complete visual verification in-game.

- Playwright’s configured Chromium executable is missing: `Browser "chromium" is not installed; expected executable at /home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome`.
- System Chromium is available at `/usr/bin/chromium` (version 157.0.8103.0); it may provide an alternative for browser verification.

1. Upgrade counter details and property props in `js/render.js`, using the existing property-specific palettes and configurations.
2. Configure or install Chromium for Playwright visual verification.
3. Capture a JPEG screenshot at no more than 1280px wide, inspect the latest screenshot, and adjust as needed.

## Relevant Files
- `js/render.js`: Isometric scene flow, depth-sorted prop rendering, shared `box()` geometry, and `drawCounter()`.
- `js/data.js`: Layouts, palettes, decor, and physical prop placements for all five properties.
- `index.html`: Game canvas and interface entry point.
- `start.sh`: Starts the game.

## Important Context
- Property IDs are `apartment`, `garage`, `lab`, `warehouse`, and `empire`.
- Props are depth-sorted by `x + y`; the counter is rendered separately via `drawCounter()`.
- No implementation changes or screenshots have been made yet.

## Objective
- Improve the physical isometric decor across all five properties, especially the counter, so it looks polished and professionally made.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game using reasonable assumptions.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs no wider than 1280px, and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Focus on the existing isometric canvas renderer and property-specific props.

## Work State
### Completed
- Upgraded `drawCounter()` with property-specific finishes, cabinet paneling, trim, a POS terminal, scale, tip jar, and take-away bags.
- Located existing property layouts and prop definitions.

### Active
- Improve the remaining physical props across the five properties.
- Complete visual verification in-game.

### Blocked
- No screenshot verification yet; Playwright’s configured Chromium executable was reported missing, though system Chromium is available at `/usr/bin/chromium`.
- A subsequent `./start.sh` attempt failed with `EADDRINUSE` on port 3000, indicating the game server may already be running.

## Next Move
1. Continue refining property-specific props in `js/render.js`.
2. Verify the running game using `/usr/bin/chromium` if needed.
3. Capture a JPEG no wider than 1280px, inspect only the latest screenshot, and adjust as needed.

- `js/render.js`: Isometric scene renderer, prop methods, and updated `drawCounter()`.
- `js/data.js`: Five property layouts, palettes, decor, and prop placements.
- `index.html`: Game canvas and interface entry point.
- `start.sh`: Starts the game.

## Important Context
- Property IDs are `apartment`, `garage`, `lab`, `warehouse`, and `empire`.

## Objective
- Improve the physical isometric decor across all five properties, especially the counter, so it looks polished and professionally made.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game using reasonable assumptions.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs no wider than 1280px, and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Focus on the existing isometric canvas renderer and property-specific props.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reworked `drawCounter()` in `js/render.js` with property-specific finishes, cabinet paneling, trim, a POS terminal, scale, tip jar, and take-away bags.
- Located existing property layouts and prop definitions.

### Active
- Improve the remaining physical props across the five properties.
- Complete visual verification in-game.

### Blocked
- Screenshot verification is still pending. Playwright’s configured Chromium executable was reported missing; system Chromium is available at `/usr/bin/chromium`.
- The game is already responding at `http://127.0.0.1:3000`; a new `./start.sh` attempt fails with `EADDRINUSE` because the port is occupied.

## Next Move
1. Refine the remaining property-specific props in `js/render.js`.
2. Verify the scene using the running game and `/usr/bin/chromium` if needed.
3. Capture a JPEG no wider than 1280px, inspect only the latest screenshot, and adjust as needed.

## Relevant Files
- `js/render.js`: Isometric scene renderer, prop methods, and updated `drawCounter()`.
- `js/data.js`: Five property layouts, palettes, decor, and prop placements.
- `js/main.js`: Game/render bootstrap and `window.__GREEN_EMPIRE__` debug handle.
- `index.html`: Game canvas and interface entry point.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Property IDs are `apartment`, `garage`, `lab`, `warehouse`, and `empire`.
- Changes are uncommitted; `js/render.js` is modified.

## Objective
- Improve the physical isometric decor across all five properties, especially the counter, so it looks polished and professionally made.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game using reasonable assumptions.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs no wider than 1280px, and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Focus on the existing isometric canvas renderer and property-specific props.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reworked `drawCounter()` in `js/render.js` with property-specific finishes, cabinet paneling, trim, a POS terminal, scale, tip jar, and take-away bags.
- Located existing property layouts and prop definitions.

### Active
- Improve the remaining physical props across the five properties.
- Complete visual verification in-game.

### Blocked
- Screenshot verification is pending; Playwright’s configured Chromium executable was reported missing, though system Chromium is available at `/usr/bin/chromium`.
- The game is already responding at `http://127.0.0.1:3000`; starting another instance fails with `EADDRINUSE`.
- A filesystem search for Playwright and the capture script exceeded its 120-second timeout.

## Next Move
1. Refine the remaining property-specific props in `js/render.js`.
2. Verify the scene using the running game and `/usr/bin/chromium` if needed.
3. Capture a JPEG no wider than 1280px, inspect only the latest screenshot, and adjust as needed.

## Relevant Files
- `js/render.js`: Isometric scene renderer, prop methods, and updated `drawCounter()`.
- `js/data.js`: Five property layouts, palettes, decor, and prop placements.
- `js/main.js`: Game/render bootstrap and `window.__GREEN_EMPIRE__` debug handle.
- `index.html`: Game canvas and interface entry point.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Property IDs are `apartment`, `garage`, `lab`, `warehouse`, and `empire`.
- Changes are uncommitted; `js/render.js` is modified.

## Objective
- Improve the physical isometric decor across all five properties, especially the counter, so it looks polished and professionally made.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game using reasonable assumptions.
- Verify with screenshots saved as JPEGs no wider than 1280px, and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Focus on the existing isometric canvas renderer and property-specific props.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reworked `drawCounter()` in `js/render.js` with property-specific finishes, cabinet paneling, trim, a POS terminal, scale, tip jar, and take-away bags.
- Added cushion piping and tuft details to `drawCouch()` in `js/render.js`.

### Active
- Improve the remaining physical props across the five properties.
- Complete visual verification in-game.

### Blocked
- Screenshot verification is pending; Playwright’s configured Chromium executable was reported missing, though system Chromium is available at `/usr/bin/chromium`.
- The game is already responding at `http://127.0.0.1:3000`; starting another instance fails with `EADDRINUSE`.
- A filesystem search for Playwright and the capture script exceeded its 120-second timeout.

## Next Move
1. Refine remaining property-specific props in `js/render.js`.
2. Verify the scene using the running game and `/usr/bin/chromium` if needed.
3. Capture a JPEG no wider than 1280px, inspect only the latest screenshot, and adjust as needed.

## Relevant Files
- `js/render.js`: Isometric scene renderer, prop methods, and updated counter/couch rendering.
- `js/data.js`: Five property layouts, palettes, decor, and prop placements.
- `js/main.js`: Game/render bootstrap and `window.__GREEN_EMPIRE__` debug handle.
- `index.html`: Game canvas and interface entry point.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Property IDs are `apartment`, `garage`, `lab`, `warehouse`, and `empire`.
- Changes are uncommitted; `js/render.js` is modified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve the physical isometric decor across all five properties, especially the counter, so it looks polished and professionally made.
- Verify the result in-game with JPEG screenshots no wider than 1280px, inspecting only the latest screenshot.

## Requirements
- Apply changes to the existing game using reasonable assumptions.
- Focus on the existing isometric canvas renderer and property-specific props.

## Decisions
- Improve property-specific props in `js/render.js`, building on the counter and couch refinements already made.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reworked `drawCounter()` with property-specific finishes, cabinet paneling, trim, POS terminal, scale, tip jar, and take-away bags.
- Added cushion piping and tuft details to `drawCouch()`.

### Active
- Refine remaining physical props across the five properties.
- Complete visual verification in-game.

### Blocked
- Screenshot verification has not yet been performed; available tools include `playwright-cli` and `/usr/bin/chromium`.

## Next Move
1. Refine the remaining props in `js/render.js`.
2. Capture and inspect the in-game scene, saving the latest screenshot as a JPEG no wider than 1280px.
3. Make any visual adjustments needed based on that screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `js/render.js`: Isometric scene renderer and property prop methods; contains the uncommitted counter and couch refinements.
- `js/data.js`: Five property layouts, palettes, decor, and prop placements.
- `js/main.js`: Renderer/game bootstrap and `window.__GREEN_EMPIRE__` debug handle.
- `index.html`: Game canvas and interface entry point.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Property IDs are `apartment`, `garage`, `lab`, `warehouse`, and `empire`.
- The game responds at `http://127.0.0.1:3000`; another server cannot start on that port while it is occupied.
- `git status` showed `js/render.js` modified; changes are uncommitted.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording

  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace

Browser sessions:

- **Core helpers:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js:216`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js#L216 ) — `spendDirty()`, `addDirty()`, and `addClean()` provide basic dirty-cash spending and cash additions.

### Unlock progression

- **Unlock checks:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js:154`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js#L154 ) — `strainUnlocked()` and `propertyAvailable()` compare the current story index with data thresholds. `frontsUnlocked()` and `staffUnlocked()` use fixed thresholds at [`game.js:165`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js#L165 ).

- For a new unlock, update the relevant data/check and verify that the associated purchase or selection method enforces it; several methods perform their own checks.

### Story mission state

- **Mission content:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/story.js:17`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/story.js#L17 ) — mission definitions hold dialogue, objectives, rewards, and choices.

- **Useful insertion points:** Add a mission in `story.js` and, if its objective type is new, extend the objective switch in `missionProgress()`. Add or adjust unlock thresholds in `data.js` and the corresponding checks in `game.js` as needed.

## Objective
- Add a redeem-code feature to Settings that grants money once per code, including a secret developer code that grants infinite money and completes/unlocks the whole story.
- Provide the user with the codes in chat after implementation.

## Requirements
- Codes can only be redeemed once.
- Include several money codes, such as one granting $1,000.
- Include a top-secret developer code for testing that grants infinite money and advances through the entire story, unlocking everything.

## Decisions
- Settings UI is built in `js/ui.js`; add the code-entry interface and redemption handling there, with persistent redeemed-code tracking in game state.

## Work State
### Completed
- Prior decor refinements in `js/render.js` were screenshot-verified at 1280×900; no visual correction was needed.

### Active
- Implement one-time redeem codes and the developer unlock code in Settings.
- Test code redemption, persistence, and full unlock/story progression.
- Tell the user the codes in chat.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add code entry and redemption feedback to `settingsHTML()` and `panelAction()` in `js/ui.js`.
2. Add persistent redeemed-code state and a safe developer grant that sets money, unlocks properties/staff/fronts/strains/upgrades, and advances story completion in `js/game.js`.
3. Test ordinary rewards and duplicate redemption across save/load, then test the developer code and share all codes with the user.

## Relevant Files
- `js/ui.js`: Settings panel markup (`settingsHTML()`) and delegated action handling (`panelAction()`).
- `js/game.js`: Game save state, cash helpers, unlock checks, and story progression.
- `js/data.js`: Property, strain, staff, front, and upgrade definitions for full unlocks.
- `js/story.js`: Mission list used to determine completed story progress.

## Important Context
- Existing saved state is version 2; `newState()` initializes `flags`, and `load()` hydrates it with `data.flags || {}`.
- Unlock checks rely on `story.idx`: properties use `reqMission`, strains use `unlockedAt`, fronts unlock at index 2, and staff at index 3.
- Settings’ action delegation uses `[data-act]`; current reset/save actions are handled in `panelAction()`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add one-time redeem codes to Settings for cash rewards, including a secret developer code that grants infinite money, completes the story, and unlocks everything.
- Share all codes in chat after implementation.

## Requirements
- Each code can be redeemed only once, with redeemed status persisted.
- Include several cash codes, including one worth $1,000.
- The developer code should make testing easier by granting infinite money and advancing through the whole story.

## Decisions
- Put the code-entry interface and redemption handling in `js/ui.js`; store redemption state in the game save.

## Work State
### Completed
- Located the Settings markup/action handlers and relevant game progression and save state.

### Active
- Implement redemption UI and persistent rewards, including the developer unlock.
- Test reward redemption, duplicate prevention across save/load, and full unlock/story completion.
- Tell the user all codes in chat.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add code entry and redemption feedback to `settingsHTML()` and `panelAction()` in `js/ui.js`.
2. Add persisted redeemed-code tracking and a developer grant in `js/game.js` that completes story progression and unlocks properties, staff, fronts, strains, and upgrades.
3. Test cash rewards, repeat redemption, save/load behavior, and developer unlock; then share all codes with the user.

## Relevant Files
- `js/ui.js`: Settings markup and delegated panel action handling.
- `js/game.js`: Save state, unlock checks, and story progression.
- `js/data.js`: Property, strain, staff, front, and upgrade definitions.
- `js/story.js`: Mission lists and story length.
- `styles.css`: Existing panel and button styling for the code-entry UI.

## Important Context
- Existing saves use version 2; `newState()` initializes `flags`, and `load()` hydrates it with `data.flags || {}`.
- Unlock checks rely on `story.idx`: properties use `reqMission`, strains use `unlockedAt`, fronts unlock at index 2, and staff at index 3.
- `js/ui.js` delegates panel actions through `[data-act]`; the Settings actions are handled in `panelAction()`.
- `js/render.js` has prior uncommitted changes from earlier work; preserve them.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Add one-time redeem codes to Settings for cash rewards, including a secret developer code that grants infinite money, completes the story, and unlocks everything.
- Share all codes in chat after implementation.

## Requirements
- Each code can be redeemed only once, with redeemed status persisted.
- Include several cash codes, including one worth $1,000.
- The developer code should make testing easier by granting infinite money and advancing through the whole story.

## Decisions
- Put the code-entry interface and redemption handling in `js/ui.js`; store redemption state in the game save.

## Work State
### Completed
- Initialized `flags.redeemedCodes` for new saves in `js/game.js`.

### Active
- Implement redemption UI and persistent rewards, including the developer unlock.
- Test cash rewards, duplicate prevention, save/load behavior, and developer unlock.
- Tell the user all codes in chat.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add code entry and redemption feedback to `settingsHTML()` and `panelAction()` in `js/ui.js`.
2. Add game redemption logic in `js/game.js`, including a developer grant that completes story progression and unlocks properties, staff, fronts, strains, and upgrades.
3. Test cash rewards, duplicate prevention, save/load persistence, and developer unlock; then share all codes with the user.

## Relevant Files
- `js/ui.js`: Settings markup and delegated panel action handling.
- `js/game.js`: Save state, redemption logic, unlock checks, and story progression.
- `js/data.js`: Property, strain, staff, front, and upgrade definitions.
- `js/story.js`: Mission lists and story length.
- `styles.css`: Existing panel and button styling.

## Important Context
- Existing saves use version 2; `load()` hydrates flags from `data.flags || {}`. Merge saved flags with defaults to retain `redeemedCodes` when loading old saves.
- Unlock checks rely on `story.idx`: properties use `reqMission`, strains use `unlockedAt`, fronts unlock at index 2, and staff at index 3.
- `js/ui.js` delegates panel actions through `[data-act]`; Settings actions are handled in `panelAction()`.
- `js/render.js` has prior uncommitted changes; preserve them.
- `js/game.js` and `js/render.js` have uncommitted changes.
